# Somatic @ Stage 8 — Preoperational

> developed 2026-07-24.

## Expression on this line

Somatic capacity at Order 7 is evaluative body awareness: the practitioner can step back from
their own body practice and ask "is this practice adequate? Is it the best way? Should I change
it?" Where Stage 7 affirmed body practice on tradition, Stage 8 evaluates body practice against
results and reason. This is the birth of body questioning: the practitioner who begins to doubt
inherited body discipline, the tradition that begins to reform, the mover who begins to compare
body practices.

The key advance is that body practice now has an evaluative structure — it can be examined,
not just followed.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** the felt capacity to evaluate one's own body practice — "is this actually the best
  way?" as a genuine question.
- **UR:** the capacity to evaluate body practice against results and reason.
- **LL:** a culture of body questioning — traditions that allow and encourage body practice
  evaluation.
- **LR:** the institutional structures (somatic therapy, body education, movement science)
  that support body practice evaluation.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** body evaluating every practice until nothing
  remains, producing body nihilism.
- **Dark allergy:** the individual who cannot or will not evaluate their
  body practice.
- **Golden addiction:** claiming to have achieved systematic body awareness (Order 8) while
  actually just questioning practices without constructing alternatives.
- **Golden allergy:** refusing to engage with body evaluation because it seems "destructive."

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Body questioning:** the practitioner examines their own body practice against results
  and reason.
- **Comparative awareness:** the practitioner recognizes that other traditions hold different
  body practices.
- **Reform capacity:** the tradition can revise its body practice in response to challenge.
